page: The Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-2400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and is bundled with 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

In standardized benchmarks, the server demonstrates strong computational and memory capabilities. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier status in stress-ng single-core CPU performance and strong status in multi-core CPU performance. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top tier, supported by strong uncached read and write memory bandwidth for large blocks. For language model workloads, the system delivers top-tier text generation speeds for small models and strong text generation speeds for medium models.

The server offers high resource density, combining substantial memory capacity with dedicated CPU allocation and fast local storage, which supports memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of a GPU. However, the 2.0 GHz clock speed may limit single-threaded execution speeds compared to higher-frequency compute-optimized instances, though this is mitigated by the top-tier single-core stress-ng benchmark results. This configuration is suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale caching layers, data processing pipelines, and medium-sized language model inference tasks.
description: The Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-2400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 12 physical cores and a 2.0 GHz clock speed, this x86_64 system includes 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in single-core CPU execution and memory scoring, alongside strong multi-core CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth. The server also demonstrates strong text generation speeds for medium-sized language models. This balanced density of memory, dedicated compute, and local NVMe storage makes the server highly suitable for memory-optimized databases, data processing pipelines, and caching layers, offering a qualitative balance of high memory capacity and dedicated CPU resources without the added cost of GPU acceleration.
